title: Ledger seed
description: Input to services/loader/seed.py. Seeds the decision ledger and commitment state. `seed_key` is a stable, human-authored handle: the loader derives a deterministic UUID from it, so re-running a seed never duplicates a row. Enum values mirror db/clickhouse/schema.sql — unlike the graph tables, `decisions` and `commitments` carry no CHECK constraints, so this contract is the only enforcement.

decisions.description: The ledger. This is the only reason a finding can say WHY.

seed_key.description: Stable handle. The decision_id UUID is derived from it, which is what makes re-seeding idempotent on an append-only MergeTree.

scene_id.description: The locked scene number, matching the graph's stable scene coordinate.

reason.description: Mandatory, never empty. schema.sql: 'the WHY'. A seeded decision with no reason is worthless to a finding.

cause_tag.description: One tap, four options. Only ever reason from 'taste'.

commitments.description: What has already been paid for. This is what makes findings rankable.

state.description: Ranking order, highest risk first: shot > built/cast > permitted/scouted > sourced > planned > none. Encoded once, in the commitmentRank UDF.

access.description: Who holds which role on this production. The policy — what each role may do — is code, in services/common/access.py; this is only the roster. No password, hash or token belongs here: the platform proves the identity (Cloud IAP), and this table says what that identity is entitled to.

subject.description: The identity the platform proved — an email address. Matched case-insensitively.

role.description: Must name a role in services/common/access.py ROLES. An unknown role denies rather than defaulting.
